risk: Capital expenditure is committed without approval, or approved on business cases that are never held to account.
audit_objective: Confirm capital spend is authorised within delegated authority and evaluated against the case that justified it.
what_to_review: Delegated authority for capital approval and its system enforcement
Business case quality — assumptions, options considered, benefits
Splitting of projects below approval thresholds
Re-approval when costs exceed the approved amount
Post-implementation review of benefits realised
procedures: Test a sample of additions to the approved capital request and the authority level applied.
Analyse spend clustering just below approval thresholds by requester and cost centre.
Compare final project cost to the approved amount and test escalation where overruns exceeded tolerance.
Select completed projects and compare realised benefits to the business case.
red_flags: Overruns absorbed without re-approval
Business cases with benefits stated but never measured
Projects split into phases to stay under a threshold
Approvals obtained after commitment
plain: Capital spending is committed years in advance and is very hard to reverse once started.

risk: Assets recorded on the register cannot be located, and assets in use are not on the register at all.
audit_objective: Confirm the fixed asset register reflects assets that physically exist and are in use.
what_to_review: Physical verification programme, coverage and independence
Asset tagging and identification
Two-way testing — register to floor and floor to register
Treatment of assets not located
Custody and responsibility for mobile and remote assets
procedures: Select assets from the register and verify physical existence; then select assets observed and trace them back to the register.
Test coverage of the verification programme and identify asset classes never verified.
Test the disposition of assets recorded as not located in previous verifications.
For mobile assets — laptops, vehicles, tools — test custody records and return on exit.
red_flags: Verification performed by the asset custodian
Assets not located simply rolled forward each year
Untagged assets in service
No verification of assets at remote or third-party sites
plain: If an asset is on the register but nobody can find it, either it was stolen or the records are wrong. Both matter.

risk: Costs are capitalised that should be expensed, or vice versa, misstating profit and the asset base.
audit_objective: Confirm the capital versus revenue distinction is applied consistently and in line with policy.
what_to_review: Capitalisation policy, thresholds and their consistent application
Treatment of repairs, refurbishment and major overhauls
Internal labour, overhead and borrowing cost capitalised
Software and development cost capitalisation criteria
Timing — capitalisation only when available for use
procedures: Sample capitalised additions and test each against the policy criteria, particularly repairs and maintenance capitalised.
Test internal labour and overhead capitalised for a supportable basis and time records.
Test software and development capitalisation against the recognition criteria, including feasibility evidence.
Test capitalisation dates against evidence the asset was ready for use.
red_flags: Repairs capitalised near year end
Internal labour capitalised at a standard percentage with no time records
Development capitalised before technical feasibility
Assets capitalised while still under construction
plain: Calling a repair an asset spreads the cost over years and makes this year's profit look better than it is.

risk: Assets are depreciated over lives that no longer reflect use, or depreciation is not charged at all on parts of the register.
audit_objective: Confirm depreciation is calculated correctly and lives and residuals remain supportable.
what_to_review: Useful lives by class and their periodic reassessment
Depreciation method and its appropriateness
Residual value assumptions against realised disposal proceeds
Assets fully depreciated but still in use
Depreciation start and stop dates
procedures: Recompute depreciation for a sample of assets and reconcile the total charge to the ledger.
Compare realised disposal proceeds to residual assumptions by class and test whether lives were reassessed.
Quantify fully depreciated assets still in use and assess whether lives were understated.
Test depreciation start dates against in-service dates.
red_flags: Lives unchanged for a decade despite changed usage
Fully depreciated assets forming a large share of the register
Residuals far above realised proceeds
Depreciation suspended without justification
evidence: Fixed asset register with depreciation detail
plain: Depreciation spreads an asset's cost over its life. Wrong life, wrong profit, every single year.

risk: Assets are disposed of below value, sold to connected parties, or removed from the register while still held.
audit_objective: Confirm disposals are authorised, competitively realised and correctly accounted.
what_to_review: Disposal authorisation and method — tender, auction, trade-in, scrap
Proceeds received, banked and recorded
Buyer identity and any connection to employees
Transfers between locations and entities
Gain and loss calculation and accounting
procedures: Test disposals for authorisation and evidence of competitive realisation.
Trace disposal proceeds to bank receipts and recompute gain or loss.
Match buyers against employee and vendor records for connections.
Test that disposed assets were removed from insurance, licensing and maintenance contracts.
red_flags: Repeat buyers across disposals
Assets written down shortly before disposal
Proceeds received in cash
Assets still insured after recorded disposal
plain: Selling company assets cheaply to someone you know is one of the oldest frauds there is.

risk: Impairment indicators are ignored, so assets that no longer generate value remain at full carrying amount.
audit_objective: Confirm impairment indicators are identified and assessments performed and supported.
what_to_review: Process for identifying impairment indicators
Cash generating unit definition and consistency
Assumptions in value-in-use models — growth, discount rate, forecast horizon
Sensitivity analysis and headroom
Reversal of prior impairments
procedures: Test whether known indicators — idle assets, loss-making units, technology change — triggered an assessment.
Recompute a value-in-use model and test the sensitivity of the conclusion to key assumptions.
Compare forecast assumptions used in impairment models to budgets used elsewhere in the business.
Test the consistency of cash generating unit definitions between periods.
red_flags: Forecasts in impairment models more optimistic than the board-approved budget
Cash generating units redefined to absorb a loss-making operation
Discount rates that fall as headroom tightens
Idle assets with no assessment
plain: When an asset stops earning its keep, the loss has already happened. Recognising it late just delays bad news.

risk: Projects remain in construction long after completion, avoiding depreciation and concealing abandoned spend.
audit_objective: Confirm assets under construction are genuinely incomplete and transferred promptly on completion.
what_to_review: Ageing of the assets under construction balance
Evidence of commissioning and transfer timing
Abandoned or stalled projects and their write-off
Costs accumulated in construction that are not capital in nature
Interest and overhead capitalised during construction
procedures: Age the construction balance and test the oldest items for evidence they are still in progress.
Physically inspect a sample of assets recorded as under construction.
Test the completeness and timing of transfers to fixed assets against commissioning evidence.
Test whether abandoned projects were written off.
red_flags: Balances in construction for more than two years
Assets in use but still recorded as under construction
Abandoned projects retained on the balance sheet
Operating costs accumulated in a construction account
plain: Projects left as 'under construction' avoid depreciation, so finished assets sometimes stay there on purpose.

risk: Leases are not identified or are misclassified, so right-of-use assets and lease liabilities are incomplete.
audit_objective: Confirm the lease population is complete and lease accounting reflects the contracts.
what_to_review: Completeness of the lease register against contracts and payments
Identification of embedded leases in service contracts
Discount rate determination
Lease modifications, extensions and termination options
Short-term and low-value exemptions applied
procedures: Search payment data for recurring rental-type payments and reconcile to the lease register.
Review significant service contracts for embedded leases.
Recompute right-of-use asset and liability for a sample of leases including options reasonably certain to be exercised.
Test the discount rates used for support.
red_flags: Leases known to operations but absent from the register
Options excluded from the term without analysis
Discount rates chosen to minimise the liability
Modifications not remeasured
plain: Rented assets now sit on the balance sheet. Leases nobody has identified mean the balance sheet is incomplete.

risk: Assets are uninsured or underinsured, and maintenance neglect shortens asset life and creates safety exposure.
audit_objective: Confirm assets are adequately insured and maintained in line with their criticality.
what_to_review: Insurance coverage against asset values and replacement cost
Reconciliation of the insured schedule to the asset register
Preventive maintenance programme and completion
Warranty tracking and claims
Critical spares and obsolescence
procedures: Reconcile the insured asset schedule to the fixed asset register and quantify uninsured or under-insured items.
Test insured values against replacement cost rather than book value.
Test preventive maintenance completion for critical assets.
Test whether warranty claims were pursued on failures within warranty.
red_flags: Insurance based on net book value
Assets acquired but never added to the policy
Maintenance deferred on critical assets
Warranty periods lapsing unclaimed
plain: Uninsured or badly maintained assets turn a single bad day into a very expensive one.

risk: There is no clear ownership of tax risk, so positions are taken across the group that nobody has assessed in aggregate.
audit_objective: Assess whether tax risk is governed, owned and reported.
what_to_review: Tax strategy, risk appetite and board oversight
Ownership of tax risk across entities and jurisdictions
Tax risk register and reporting to the audit committee
Resourcing and technical capability
Use and oversight of external advisers
procedures: Review the tax risk register against issues identified in the audit and assess completeness.
Test whether material tax positions were reported to the audit committee.
Assess whether advice received from advisers was acted upon or quietly shelved.
Test that each jurisdiction has an identified owner for tax compliance.
red_flags: Tax risk register listing only routine compliance
Advice obtained and then not followed
Jurisdictions with no named owner
No tax item reaching the audit committee in a year
plain: Without someone clearly owning tax risk, positions get taken across the group that nobody has assessed together.

risk: Corporate tax returns are filed late or on positions that cannot be supported, generating assessments, interest and penalties.
audit_objective: Confirm direct tax obligations are met accurately and on time in every jurisdiction.
what_to_review: Completeness of the filing calendar across all entities
Filing and payment timeliness
Support for deductions, reliefs and losses claimed
Reconciliation of the tax charge to the accounting profit
Correspondence and open enquiries with authorities
procedures: Build the obligation calendar independently from the entity register and compare to the one in use.
Test filing and payment dates against deadlines and quantify penalties and interest.
Test support for significant deductions and reliefs claimed.
Reconcile the effective tax rate and test the explanation for material reconciling items.
red_flags: Entities discovered to have filing obligations nobody tracked
Repeated late filings in one jurisdiction
Losses carried forward without evidence of availability
Effective rate movements unexplained
plain: Corporate tax filed late or wrongly attracts interest and penalties, and authorities can look back several years.

risk: VAT, GST or sales tax is charged, recovered or remitted incorrectly across large transaction volumes, so small errors become material.
audit_objective: Confirm indirect tax is applied correctly at transaction level and returns are complete.
what_to_review: Tax code determination logic in the systems
Treatment of cross-border, exempt and zero-rated supplies
Input tax recovery and partial exemption calculations
Manual overrides of tax codes
Reconciliation of returns to the ledger
procedures: Sample transactions across supply types and re-perform the tax determination.
Analyse manual tax code overrides by user and value.
Recompute the input tax recovery or partial exemption calculation.
Reconcile returns filed to the general ledger and test differences.
red_flags: Tax codes overridden routinely at invoice entry
Recovery claimed on blocked categories
Cross-border supplies defaulting to domestic treatment
Return to ledger differences carried forward
plain: Sales tax and VAT are applied to enormous numbers of transactions, so a small error repeated becomes a large bill.

risk: Payments to employees and contractors are misclassified, creating employment tax liabilities and worker status exposure.
audit_objective: Confirm employment taxes are correctly applied, including on benefits and contractor arrangements.
what_to_review: Worker status determinations for contractors and consultants
Benefits in kind identification and reporting
Expense reimbursements treated as non-taxable
Termination payments and their tax treatment
Cross-border and mobile employee obligations
procedures: Sample contractors and test the worker status determination against the substance of the engagement.
Test expense categories treated as non-taxable for correct treatment.
Test benefit reporting completeness against payroll and procurement data — company cars, health cover, allowances.
Test the tax treatment of termination settlements.
red_flags: Long-serving contractors working like employees
Round-sum allowances paid untaxed
Benefits identified only from the payroll system
Mobile employees with no jurisdiction analysis
plain: Treating someone as a contractor when they work like an employee creates back-tax liabilities plus penalties.

risk: Intragroup transactions are priced without support, exposing the group to adjustment, double taxation and penalties.
audit_objective: Confirm intragroup pricing follows policy and is documented to the standard each jurisdiction requires.
what_to_review: Transfer pricing policy and its application in practice
Local file, master file and country-by-country reporting
Benchmarking studies and their currency
Intragroup service charges and evidence of benefit
Funding, royalties and licence arrangements
procedures: Test whether intragroup transactions were actually priced per policy by recomputing a sample.
Test documentation exists and is current for each jurisdiction with a requirement.
Test service charges for evidence the recipient benefited, not merely that cost was allocated.
Review benchmarking studies for age and comparability.
red_flags: Documentation prepared long after year end
Service charges allocated by formula with no benefit evidence
Benchmarks several years old
Pricing that differs from the stated policy
plain: When group companies charge each other, tax authorities want proof the price was fair. No proof means an adjustment.

risk: The tax provision and deferred tax balances are misstated because positions and temporary differences are not tracked.
audit_objective: Confirm tax balances in the accounts are supported and complete.
what_to_review: Current tax provision support and reconciliation to returns filed
Deferred tax asset and liability calculation and temporary difference tracking
Recoverability of deferred tax assets and the forecasts supporting them
Uncertain tax positions and their measurement
Prior year adjustments and their causes
procedures: Reconcile the provision to returns subsequently filed and test the causes of significant true-ups.
Recompute deferred tax on a sample of temporary differences.
Test the forecast supporting deferred tax asset recognition against board-approved projections.
Test the measurement of uncertain tax positions against authority correspondence.
red_flags: Large recurring prior year adjustments
Deferred tax assets supported by forecasts no one else uses
Uncertain positions not provided for despite live enquiries
Temporary differences tracked in a single spreadsheet
plain: The tax numbers in the accounts are estimates too, and they depend on forecasts that may not hold.

risk: Authority enquiries are handled inconsistently and the same issues recur across jurisdictions and years.
audit_objective: Assess how tax enquiries are managed and whether findings drive change.
what_to_review: Tracking of open enquiries, assessments and appeals
Ownership and consistency of responses
Provisioning for assessments raised
Root cause analysis on findings and remediation
Lessons applied across other jurisdictions
procedures: Review open enquiries and test whether provisions reflect the exposure.
Trace closed enquiry findings to remediation actions and test whether they were implemented.
Test whether findings in one jurisdiction were assessed for relevance in others.
Test the timeliness of responses against authority deadlines.
red_flags: Same finding raised in successive audits
Assessments settled with no root cause work
Responses missing deadlines
Provisions raised only after assessment is final
plain: When a tax authority finds something, the same issue usually exists elsewhere in the group.

risk: Tax calculations depend on manual extracts and spreadsheets nobody controls, so errors are undetectable.
audit_objective: Assess the integrity of the data and tools used to calculate and report tax.
what_to_review: Source data quality feeding tax calculations
Reliance on spreadsheets and end user computing
Tax engine configuration and change control
Access to tax master data and rate tables
Audit trail from tax return back to source transactions
procedures: Trace a tax return figure back to source transactions and assess the effort required — poor traceability is itself a finding.
Test controls over the spreadsheets used in tax computation, including version control and formula integrity.
Test change control over tax engine configuration and rate tables.
Test who can amend tax master data.
red_flags: Tax computed in an unversioned spreadsheet
Rate tables amended without change control
No audit trail from return to ledger
One person holding all tax model knowledge
evidence: Tax engine configuration and change logs
plain: Tax is often calculated in spreadsheets nobody controls, which makes errors invisible until an authority finds them.
